proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(L=\log(en)\) and \(\widetilde Y=Y/2\).  We invoke the established
construction
\(\mathtt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier/
thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\) only for
its explicit clipped Chebyshev factorial estimator and its proved pilot and
approximation certificates.  Its hypotheses hold after this rescaling.  In
fact, the cell-mean envelope gives
\[
 \left|E_P[\widetilde Y\mid A=a,X=k]\right|
 =\frac{|\mu_{ak}|}{2}\le \frac M2.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover, Cauchy--Schwarz and the conditional fourth-moment condition in the
definition of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) give
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_P\!\left[\left(\widetilde Y-\frac{\mu_{ak}}2\right)^2
       \middle|A=a,X=k\right]
 &\le
 \left\{E_P\!\left[\left(\widetilde Y-\frac{\mu_{ak}}2\right)^4
       \middle|A=a,X=k\right]\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &=\frac14
 \left\{E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac{M^2}{4}.
 \end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
The fixed-overlap hypothesis is unchanged by rescaling, and independence of
the pilot and estimation folds follows from iid sampling.  Thus the cited
construction may be applied to \(\widetilde Y\), after which its output is
multiplied by two.

We next verify, rather than assume, the asserted four-coordinate form.  For a
cell \(k\), write
\[
 x_0=p_k(1-\pi_k),\qquad x_1=p_k\pi_k,\qquad
 z_a=x_a\mu_{ak},\qquad p_k=x_0+x_1.
\tag{3}
\]
The cited construction uses constants
\[
 K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor,\qquad
 \alpha_0=\min\left\{1,(64\log6)^{-1},(512D_6)^{-1}\right\},
 \qquad D_6=8\log(27/4),
\tag{4}
\]
the light-mass scale \(B=4096L/m_1\), where \(m_1\asymp n\) is the
estimation-fold size, and pilot threshold \(256L\).  Select the numerical
coefficient in \(L_n\) so that \(c_L\ge\alpha_0\); then \(K\le L_n\).
For the Chebyshev polynomial \(T_K\), define the polynomials, with their
continuous values at zero,
\[
 H_K(t)=\frac{1-T_K(1-2t)}{2K^2},\qquad
 E_K(t)=\frac{H_K(t)}t,\qquad
 G_K(t)=\frac{1-E_K(t)}t.
\tag{5}
\]
The identities \(T_K(1)=1\) and \(T'_K(1)=K^2\) show that both divisions in
(5) are exact polynomial divisions.  Since
\(T_K(\cos\vartheta)=\cos(K\vartheta)\), for \(0\le t\le1\),
\[
 0\le t\{1-tG_K(t)\}=H_K(t)\le K^{-2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Also, \(G_K\) has degree at most \(K-2\).  Hence
\[
 q_a(x_0,x_1)=\frac{x_0+x_1}{B}G_K(x_a/B)
\tag{7}
\]
has total degree at most \(K-1\le L_n-1\), and therefore
\[
 (x_0,z_0,x_1,z_1)\longmapsto
 z_1q_1(x_0,x_1)-z_0q_0(x_0,x_1)
 \in\mathscr Q_{L_n}.
\tag{8}
\]
This is the required four-coordinate rewrite on every dyadic slice of
\(\mathcal K_{\epsilon,M}(B)\).

Let \(\mathcal A\) be the pilot-good event from the cited construction.  On
\(\mathcal A\), every pilot-selected light cell obeys \(p_k\le B/4\).
For such a cell, fixed overlap yields \(x_a\ge\epsilon p_k\), while
\(0\le x_a/B\le1\).  Equations (3), (6), and the cell-mean envelope imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 \left|p_k\mu_{ak}-\frac{p_kz_a}{B}G_K(x_a/B)\right|
 &=p_k|\mu_{ak}|\frac{H_K(x_a/B)}{x_a/B}\\
 &\le \frac{MB}{\epsilon K^2}.
 \end{split}
\tag{9}
\]
Condition on the pilot sample.  An ordered distinct-index falling-factorial
term with one outcome mark is unbiased for the corresponding monomial
\(z_ap_kx_a^j\): after expansion over distinct indices, independence makes
its expectation the product of the one-observation mass and mark moments.
Linearity of this identity, first conditionally on the pilot and then
unconditionally, and summation of (9) over the two arms and at most \(d\)
selected cells give
\[
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right]\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A}\right|
 \le \frac{2MdB}{\epsilon K^2}.
\tag{10}
\]
The cited pilot certificate, applied under fixed overlap and
\(d\le c_\epsilon nL\), states after decreasing \(c_\epsilon\) if necessary
that
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(\mathcal A^c)
 \le2d\exp(-c_\epsilon256L)\le C_\epsilon n^{-6}.
\tag{11}
\]
Both the factorial output and its target contribution are clipped at the
source envelope, so (11) contributes at most \(C_\epsilon Mn^{-6}\) to
(10).  The same calculation is precisely the cited pilot-misclassification
bound.  Since \(B\asymp L/n\), \(K\asymp L\), and \(L\ge1\), (10)--(11)
yield, after enlarging the constant for the finitely many rows for which
\(K<2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right]\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\tag{12}
\]
Finally, the Chebyshev recurrence has \(O(L_n^2)\) coefficients per cell;
the fixed four-coordinate bookkeeping, falling-factorial recurrence, zero
fallbacks, and clipping therefore require \(O(dL_n^2)\), hence
\(O(dL_n^3)\), arithmetic operations.  Rescaling the single mark by one half
and multiplying the final output by two preserves every expectation identity,
zero fallback, clipping rule, and pilot certificate.  This proves all parts
of the lemma.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Finite-sample coverage and the sharp expected-radius bound for an explicit heavy--light interval on the unrestricted global class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The selected-factorial rare radius remains unresolved in the sibling-owned rare-tail question, and the heavy winsorized Gaussian/fallback radius is still not an explicit sample map. The exact all-heavy center and variance override does not furnish either tail certificate.
open_obligations.attempted: I combined the proved light-branch bias with the exact all-heavy override and decomposed the remaining error into light fluctuation, heavy fluctuation, truncation, and pilot terms. Only the deterministic light bias and the local all-heavy bridge follow from the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved light-approximation lemma supplies
\[
 \left|E\widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -E\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\]
The frozen heavy--light handle also gives an exact center and variance
identity on the all-heavy pilot event.  If explicit light and heavy radii
satisfied their allocated conditional tail bounds and had expected sizes
\(C_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\) and
\(C_{\epsilon,\alpha}Mn^{-1/2}\), respectively, the triangle inequality and
the allocation of the noncoverage probability would prove the target, and
intersection with \([-2M,2M]\) would not enlarge length.  The frozen core
does not define radii with those properties, so this implication cannot be
turned into a proof of the stated interval theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A certified outward enclosure of the actual statistical score roots and the asserted bit complexity.
open_obligations.obstruction: No valid exact-real heavy score is defined, and the proposed light-score handle supplies neither a proved monotone inversion equation nor a positive root-slope modulus. Therefore outward score evaluation cannot be converted uniformly into endpoint accuracy.
open_obligations.attempted: I propagated the coefficient and factorial magnitude bounds through the declared working-precision envelope and verified deterministic interval inclusion and length inflation. The root-enclosure induction stops at the absent monotonicity and slope certificate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let the exact-real interval be \([L,U]\).  If outward interval arithmetic
returns \(\widetilde L\le L\le U\le\widetilde U\) with
\(L-\widetilde L\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\) and
\(\widetilde U-U\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\), then deterministically
\[
 [L,U]\subseteq[\widetilde L,\widetilde U],\qquad
 (\widetilde U-\widetilde L)-(U-L)\le2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}.
\]
Thus coverage is monotone under the certified enlargement.  The banked
coefficient bound and the declared working precision control the arithmetic
magnitudes of the Chebyshev and factorial recurrences.  What is unavailable
is a defined monotone statistical score with a positive root-slope modulus;
without it, score-enclosure error cannot be converted into the asserted
endpoint error or bisection count.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The matching minimax upper inequality and certified attainment at the candidate frontier scale.
open_obligations.obstruction: The same-class converse is established, but the only fully certified upper procedure in the frozen core is the deterministic range interval. The proposed heavy--light radii have no finite-sample tail theorem, so the range upper bound cannot be sharpened to the asserted rate.
open_obligations.attempted: I combined the established converse with the deterministic range interval and checked that this gives the best currently closed two-sided bracket. The formal implication from a sharp honest upper theorem was also verified, but that upstream premise remains unproved.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The established same-class testing converse and the deterministic interval
\([-2M,2M]\) give the closed bracket
\[
 c_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}
 \le\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\le4M.
\]
The upper interval is measurable, has uniform coverage one, and has length
\(4M\).  The matching upper inequality of order \(r_{n,d,M}\) and its
finite-precision attainment would follow from the two still-unproved upstream
targets, but neither follows from the converse or the range interval.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The heavy--light radius expansion to the Gaussian critical value.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact all-heavy override transfers the established saturated one-step center, variance, and central-limit conclusions with probability tending to one. It imposes no formula or identity for the total radius, and no globally honest Gaussian/fallback hybrid score has been defined or proved.
open_obligations.attempted: I transferred every center and variance conclusion on the established all-heavy event and isolated the radius assertion as the only remaining local clause. Fixed overlap, fourth moments, balance, and nondegenerate efficient variance do not determine an unspecified confidence radius.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let
\[
 \mathcal H_n=
 \left\{\min_{a\in\{0,1\},\,1\le k\le d_n}
 N_{ak}^{(0)}>256\log(en)\right\}.
\]
The established all-heavy pilot lemma gives
\(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)=o(1)\).  On \(\mathcal H_n\), the frozen
heavy--light handle imposes the exact identities
\[
 (\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}})
 =(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}).
\]
Consequently the established saturated one-step benchmark transfers the
heavy--light center expansion, the center comparison, variance-ratio
consistency, and the centered Gaussian limit: equality on events whose
probabilities tend to one preserves each convergence-in-probability and
weak-convergence assertion.  No corresponding identity is imposed on
\(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}\).  Hence the claimed expansion of that radius to
the Gaussian critical radius remains unproved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The heavy--light radius comparison needed for endpoint equivalence, together with the global honesty and numerical conclusions cited by the theorem.
open_obligations.obstruction: Center and variance comparison follow on the all-heavy event, but the total heavy--light radius has no proved Gaussian/fallback formula. Without its little-oh comparison to the Gaussian radius, endpoint equivalence cannot follow; global honesty and numerical transfer also depend on separate unresolved targets.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced the endpoint claim to the sum of center and radius differences and proved that lower- and upper-endpoint projection onto the causal range is one-Lipschitz. This closes the boundary argument and leaves only the unavailable radius and upstream coverage premises.
open_obligations.partial_result:
On the balanced triangular class, the all-heavy identity and the two
established local results imply
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}
 =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}}
 -\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).
\]
The second relation uses the positive lower and finite upper bounds on
\(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/M^2\), so division and the square-root map are
legitimate.  Were the missing radius relation
\[
 \widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}
 -z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/n}
 =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})
\]
available, each unprojected endpoint difference would be
\(o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\).  The maps
\(x\mapsto\max\{-2M,x\}\) and \(x\mapsto\min\{2M,x\}\) are
one-Lipschitz, so projection would preserve that order, including at the
boundary.  This proves the projection reduction but not the missing radius,
global honesty, or numerical assertions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The heavy--light Wald-radius and endpoint part of the fixed-alphabet reduction.
open_obligations.obstruction: Fixed alphabet makes the all-heavy complement exponentially rare and validates the saturated one-step benchmark, but it neither defines the heavy--light radius nor forces its critical value to be Gaussian.
open_obligations.attempted: I specialized the balanced triangular assumptions to fixed alphabet and transferred the proved one-step center, variance, and Gaussian conclusions through the exact all-heavy override. No radius assertion can be transferred from an identity that does not include the radius.
open_obligations.partial_result:
If \(d_n=d\) is fixed, then \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the balanced lower bound remains
\(p_k\ge c_0/d\), and the efficient variance remains in
\([v_0M^2,v_1M^2]\).  The established saturated one-step benchmark therefore
gives its efficient-influence-function expansion, ratio-consistent variance,
and Gaussian limit.  The all-heavy pilot failure probability is exponentially
small, so the frozen exact override transfers the same center and variance
conclusions to the heavy--light outputs.  Fixed alphabet does not define the
heavy--light radius or imply its Gaussian critical-value expansion, and hence
does not complete the stated Wald-endpoint reduction.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  By
\(\texttt{def:control-arm-zero-binary-subclass}\), this law belongs to
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), satisfies
\(Y(0)=0\) almost surely by
\(\texttt{ass:control-arm-zero-subclass}\), and satisfies
\(Y(1)\in\{0,M\}\) almost surely by
\(\texttt{ass:treated-binary-subclass}\).  If \(p_k>0\), then
\(\texttt{ass:fixed-overlap}\) gives
\[
 P(A=0,X=k)=p_k(1-\pi_k)\ge \epsilon p_k>0.
\tag{1}
\]
On \(\{A=0\}\), consistency
\(\texttt{ass:consistency}\) and \(Y(0)=0\) give \(Y=Y(0)=0\)
almost surely.  The conditional mean is therefore well defined on the event
in (1), and
\[
 \mu_{0k}=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]=0.
\tag{2}
\]
Substituting (2) into the identifying equality in
\(\texttt{def:ate-functional}\), and then using
\(\texttt{def:one-arm-functional}\), yields
\[
 \tau(P)
 =\sum_{k=1}^d p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 =\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\mu_{1k}
 =\psi_1(P).
\tag{3}
\]

We next verify the claimed embedding and its risk scaling.  Consider any
unit-scale law in the binary one-arm hard family to which the cited result
\(\texttt{lem:zeng-one-arm-lower}\) applies.  Write its cell masses and
propensities as \(p_k\) and \(\pi_k\), and write
\(m_k\in[0,1]\) for the success probability of its binary treated outcome
\(B\in\{0,1\}\) in cell \(k\).  Construct a full-data law
\(P^{(M)}\) as follows.  Retain the law of \(X\), draw
\(A\mid X=k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\), draw
\(B\mid X=k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(m_k)\) independently of \(A\)
conditional on \(X\), and set
\[
 Y(0)=0,\qquad Y(1)=MB,
 \qquad Y=Y(A).
\tag{4}
\]
Thus (4) gives consistency, while the stipulated conditional independence
gives \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\), as required by
\(\texttt{ass:conditional-exchangeability}\).  Cell masses and propensities
are unchanged, so the source family's overlap bounds imply
\(\texttt{ass:fixed-overlap}\).  For every positive-mass cell,
\[
 \mu_{0k}=0,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1k}=Mm_k,
 \qquad
 |\mu_{ak}|\le M,
\tag{5}
\]
which verifies \(\texttt{ass:cell-mean-envelope}\).  For the control arm the
conditional fourth central moment is zero.  For the treated arm, conditional
independence in (4) and \(|B-m_k|\le1\) imply
\[
 E_{P^{(M)}}[(Y-\mu_{1k})^4\mid X=k,A=1]
 =M^4E[(B-m_k)^4\mid X=k]
 \le M^4.
\tag{6}
\]
Hence \(\texttt{ass:conditional-fourth-moment}\) also holds.  Equations
(4)--(6), together with \(\texttt{def:global-law-class}\) and
\(\texttt{def:control-arm-zero-binary-subclass}\), prove
\[
 P^{(M)}\in
 \mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}.
\tag{7}
\]
Moreover, (3) and (5) give the exact target scaling
\[
 \tau(P^{(M)})
 =M\sum_{k=1}^d p_km_k
 =M\psi_1(P^{(1)}),
\tag{8}
\]
where \(P^{(1)}\) denotes the corresponding unit-scale one-arm law.  Thus
every separation between two source values of \(\psi_1\) is multiplied by
\(M\) after embedding.

For completeness, let \(T_M\) be the deterministic sample transformation
that replaces each unit-scale observed binary outcome by its product with
\(M\), leaving \(X\) and \(A\) unchanged.  By (4), applying \(T_M\) to an
iid observed sample with law \(Q_{P^{(1)}}^{(n)}\) has exactly the observed
sample law
\(Q_{P^{(M)}}^{(n)}\).  Given any measurable ATE estimator
\(\widehat\tau\), define on the source experiment
\[
 \widehat\psi(D)=M^{-1}\widehat\tau(T_M D).
\tag{9}
\]
The division in (9) is valid because \(M\ge1\).  From (8)--(9), for every
source law,
\[
 E_{Q_{P^{(1)}}^{(n)}}[(\widehat\psi-\psi_1(P^{(1)}))^2]
 =M^{-2}E_{Q_{P^{(M)}}^{(n)}}
   [\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P^{(M)})\}^2].
\tag{10}
\]
The estimator in (9) is an admissible estimator in the source experiment.
Therefore \(\texttt{lem:zeng-one-arm-lower}\), followed by (7) and (10),
implies for every \(\widehat\tau\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\}^2]
 &\ge
 \sup_{P^{(1)}\ \mathrm{in\ the\ source\ hard\ family}}
 E_{Q_{P^{(M)}}^{(n)}}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P^{(M)})\}^2]\\
 &\ge c_{\epsilon}M^2
 \left\{n^{-1}+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
 \end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
throughout the dimension range stated by that cited lemma.  Taking the
infimum of (11) over all measurable \(\widehat\tau\) establishes the claimed
ATE point-estimation lower scale by subclass restriction.

Finally, (11) is only a minimax squared-error statement.  Its derivation does
not assert that the source lower-bound prior puts its ATE values in two
separated target sets after any conditioning, nor does it bound total
variation between the corresponding prior-predictive observed laws.  Those
are distinct hypotheses of the interval testing argument in
\(\texttt{lem:coverage-testing-inequality}\).  Accordingly, this proposition
does not by itself imply a confidence-length lower bound; the direct
target-set separation and prior-predictive total-variation calculation used
for that purpose are supplied separately in
\(\texttt{thm:same-class-testing-converse}\), exactly as the final sentence
of the proposition states.

All unqualified expectations and probabilities below are taken under the row
law \(P_n\) and its iid sample law \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\), respectively.  Write
\[
 p_{k,n}=P_n(X=k),\qquad
 \pi_{k,n}=P_n(A=1\mid X=k),\qquad
 \sigma_{ak,n}^2
 =E_{P_n}\!\left[(Y-\mu_{ak,n})^2\mid X=k,A=a\right].
\]
The lower mass condition gives \(p_{k,n}\ge c_0/d>0\), and fixed overlap
then gives positive probability to both arm--cell events, so every displayed
conditional quantity is defined.  By the conditional fourth-moment
assumption and
\(\{E(Z^2)\}^2\le E(Z^4)\), which follows from
\(E[(Z^2-EZ^2)^2]\ge0\),
\[
 \sigma_{ak,n}^2\le M^2.                                           \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 h_{k,n}=\mu_{1k,n}-\mu_{0k,n}-\tau(P_n),\qquad
 V_n=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n),\qquad \phi_n=\phi_{P_n}.
\]
The identifying equality in \(def:ate\text{-}functional\) gives
\(\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}h_{k,n}=0\).  Conditional on \(X=k\), each outcome
residual in \(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\) has mean zero,
and the treated and control residual terms have product zero because
\(A(1-A)=0\).  Expanding the square and then averaging over \(X\) therefore
gives
\[
 V_n=\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\left\{
 h_{k,n}^2+\frac{\sigma_{1k,n}^2}{\pi_{k,n}}
              +\frac{\sigma_{0k,n}^2}{1-\pi_{k,n}}
 \right\}.                                                         \tag{2}
\]
Every term in braces is nonnegative.  Since fixed overlap implies
\(0<\pi_{k,n}<1\), for \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\sigma_{ak,n}^2\le V_n,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}h_{k,n}^2\le V_n.                             \tag{3}
\]

We first analyze the saturated one-step construction.  For validation fold
\(I_s\), define its training size \(m_{s,n}=n-|I_s|\) and the training
arm--cell count
\[
 \overline N_{ak}^{(-s)}
 =\sum_{j\notin I_s}\mathbf 1\{X_j=k,A_j=a\}.
\]
Also set
\[
 q_{1k,n}=p_{k,n}\pi_{k,n},\qquad
 q_{0k,n}=p_{k,n}(1-\pi_{k,n}).
\]
The mass lower bound and fixed overlap imply
\[
 q_{ak,n}\ge q_*:=\frac{c_0\epsilon}{d}>0.                          \tag{4}
\]
Because \(K_0\) is fixed and the fold sizes differ by at most one, there is
a constant \(c_{\mathrm{tr}}>0\), depending only on \(K_0\), such that
\(m_{s,n}\ge c_{\mathrm{tr}}n\) for all folds and all sufficiently large
\(n\).  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), then
\[
 P(N=0)=(1-q)^m\le e^{-mq}.                                        \tag{5}
\]
When \(mq\ge1\), splitting according to \(N\ge mq/2\) and applying
Markov's inequality to \((N-mq)^2\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{N>0\}}{N}\right]
 &\le \frac{2}{mq}+P(0<N<mq/2)\\
 &\le \frac{2}{mq}+\frac{4\operatorname{Var}(N)}{m^2q^2}
 \le\frac{6}{mq}.
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{6}
\]

Let
\[
 e_{ak}^{(-s)}=\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak,n},\qquad
 \delta_k^{(-s)}=\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_{k,n}.
\]
Conditional on \(\overline N_{ak}^{(-s)}>0\), the outcome estimate in
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) is a mean of that many independent
draws from the arm--cell law; it is unbiased and has conditional variance
\(\sigma_{ak,n}^2/\overline N_{ak}^{(-s)}\).  On the empty-cell event its
zero fallback has squared error at most \(M^2\) by the cell-mean envelope.
Equations \((4)\)--\((6)\) therefore imply, uniformly over the fixed set of
\((a,k,s)\),
\[
 E[(e_{ak}^{(-s)})^2]
 \le \frac{C\sigma_{ak,n}^2}{n}+CM^2e^{-cn}.                        \tag{7}
\]
For the propensity estimate, condition instead on the number of training
observations with \(X=k\).  On a nonempty cell the empirical treatment
fraction is unbiased with conditional variance at most the reciprocal of
that count; on an empty cell its squared error is at most one.  Clipping
cannot increase distance from
\(\pi_{k,n}\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), because this interval is contained
in the clipping interval \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\).  Applying
\((5)\)--\((6)\) with \(p_{k,n}\ge c_0/d\) gives
\[
 E[(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2]\le \frac Cn+Ce^{-cn}.                       \tag{8}
\]
Here and below \(c,C>0\) may depend on
\((d,c_0,\epsilon,K_0)\), but not on \(n\) or on the row law.

Define the oracle uncentered score
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \psi_n(O)
 &=\mu_{1X,n}-\mu_{0X,n}
 +\frac{A(Y-\mu_{1X,n})}{\pi_{X,n}}
 -\frac{(1-A)(Y-\mu_{0X,n})}{1-\pi_{X,n}}\\
 &=\tau(P_n)+\phi_n(O).
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{9}
\]
For \(i\in I_s\), put \(D_{i,s}=\widehat\psi_i-\psi_n(O_i)\).
Iid sampling and deterministic sample splitting make \(O_i\) independent
of the training sample \(\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}=(O_j:j\notin I_s)\).
Direct substitution in the two scores and conditional expectation over
\(O_i\) give
\[
 E[D_{i,s}\mid X_i=k,\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]
 =\delta_k^{(-s)}\left\{
 \frac{e_{1k}^{(-s)}}{\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 +\frac{e_{0k}^{(-s)}}{1-\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 \right\}.                                                        \tag{10}
\]
Both denominators are at least \(\epsilon/2\).  If
\(B_{s,n}=E[D_{i,s}\mid\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]\), then Cauchy--Schwarz,
\((7)\), and \((8)\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E|B_{s,n}|
 &\le \frac{2}{\epsilon}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}
    \{E[(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2]E[(e_{ak}^{(-s)})^2]\}^{1/2}\\
 &\le \frac Cn\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\sigma_{ak,n}
       +CMe^{-cn}\\
 &\le C\left\{\frac{\sqrt{V_n}}n+Me^{-cn}\right\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{11}
\]
The last line uses \(\sum_kp_{k,n}=1\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and \((3)\).
The mean envelope and the identifying formula give \(|h_{k,n}|\le4M\).
The inequality \((x_1+x_2+x_3)^4\le27(x_1^4+x_2^4+x_3^4)\), the
conditional fourth-moment bound, and overlap then give
\[
 E_{P_n}[\phi_n(O)^4]\le C_\epsilon M^4,
 \qquad V_n\le C_\epsilon M^2.                                    \tag{12}
\]
Consequently \((11)\) and Markov's inequality show
\(\sqrt n B_{s,n}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1)\), uniformly over the fixed number
of folds.

Before taking conditional expectation in \((10)\), the same score
substitution, the clipping bounds, and
\((x_1+\cdots+x_r)^2\le r\sum_jx_j^2\) give
\[
 E[D_{i,s}^2\mid\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}]
 \le C\sum_{k=1}^d p_{k,n}\left[
 (e_{1k}^{(-s)})^2+(e_{0k}^{(-s)})^2
 +(\delta_k^{(-s)})^2
       (\sigma_{1k,n}^2+\sigma_{0k,n}^2)
 \right].                                                         \tag{13}
\]
Taking expectations and applying \((3)\), \((7)\), and \((8)\) yields
\[
 E[D_{i,s}^2]\le \frac{CV_n}{n}+CM^2e^{-cn}=o(M^2).                \tag{14}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n^{(-s)}\), the centered variables
\(D_{i,s}-B_{s,n}\), \(i\in I_s\), are independent.  For each fold,
conditional variance and \((14)\) give
\[
 E\!\left[\left\{\frac1{\sqrt n}
   \sum_{i\in I_s}(D_{i,s}-B_{s,n})\right\}^2\right]
 \le \frac{|I_s|}{n}E[D_{i,s}^2]=o(M^2).
\]
Together with \(\sqrt nB_{s,n}=o_P(1)\) and fixed \(K_0\), the exact
decomposition
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_{i,s}
 =\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\left\{
   \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\in I_s}(D_{i,s}-B_{s,n})
   +\frac{|I_s|}{\sqrt n}B_{s,n}\right\}
\]
therefore proves
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_{i,s}
 =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).                                             \tag{15}
\]
Combining \((9)\), \((15)\), and the definition of
\(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)
  +o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(1).                                            \tag{16}
\]
The leading sum has mean zero and variance \(V_n\) by \((2)\).  Since
\(M\) is fixed and the premise \(V_n/M^2\to0\) implies \(V_n\to0\),
Chebyshev's inequality applied to the leading sum and \((16)\) imply
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}
 \longrightarrow0                                                  \tag{17}
\]
in \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability.

For the variance estimator, independence and \((12)\) give
\[
 E\!\left[\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)^2-V_n\right\}^2\right]
 \le \frac{E[\phi_n(O)^4]}n
 \le \frac{C_\epsilon M^4}{n}.                                    \tag{18}
\]
Averaging \((14)\) over observations and applying Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,s(i)}^2=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M^2),           \tag{19}
\]
where \(s(i)\) is the fold containing \(i\).  Centering at the empirical
mean minimizes the empirical sum of squares, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\le\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}
 &\le\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\psi_i-\tau(P_n)\}^2\\
 &\le\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_n(O_i)^2
     +\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,s(i)}^2.
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{20}
\]
Equations \((18)\)--\((20)\) and \(V_n/M^2\to0\) prove
\[
 \widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2\longrightarrow0                     \tag{21}
\]
in probability.

It remains to transfer \((17)\) and \((21)\) to the heavy--light outputs.
Let
\[
 \mathcal H_n
 =\left\{\min_{a\in\{0,1\},\,1\le k\le d}N_{ak}^{(0)}
             >256\log(en)\right\}
 =\{\widehat{\mathcal L}=\varnothing\}.
\]
Because the pilot fold sizes differ from \(n/K_0\) by at most one, there is
\(c_{\mathrm{pil}}>0\), depending only on \(K_0\), such that
\(|I_0|\ge c_{\mathrm{pil}}n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Each
\(N_{ak}^{(0)}\) is binomial with mean
\(\nu_{ak,n}=|I_0|q_{ak,n}\ge c_{\mathrm{pil}}q_*n\), and hence
\(256\log(en)\le\nu_{ak,n}/2\) eventually.  For
\(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), exponential Markov with
\(t=\log2\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(N\le mq/2)
 &\le e^{tmq/2}E[e^{-tN}]\\
 &=e^{tmq/2}(1-q+qe^{-t})^m\\
 &\le\exp\{mq[t/2-(1-e^{-t})]\}
 \le e^{-mq/8},
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{22}
\]
because \(1-u\le e^{-u}\) and \((1-\log2)/2>1/8\).  A union bound over
the \(2d\) pilot arm--cells and \((4)\) therefore gives
\[
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)
 \le2d\exp\!\left(-\frac{c_{\mathrm{pil}}c_0\epsilon}{8d}n\right)
 =o(1).                                                            \tag{23}
\]
The all-heavy clause of
\(def:robust\text{-}heavy\text{-}light\text{-}interval\text{-}handle\)
is the exact sample identity
\[
 (\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}})
 =(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}})
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal H_n.                                     \tag{24}
\]
Thus, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\sqrt n
   |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)|>r\right)
 &\le Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)
  +Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\sqrt n
   |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)|>r\right),\\
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/M^2>r\right)
 &\le Q_{P_n}^{(n)}(\mathcal H_n^c)
  +Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\!\left(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2>r\right).
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{25}
\]
Equations \((17)\), \((21)\), and \((23)\) prove both heavy--light
conclusions.  Notice that this transfer uses no asserted property of either
proposed confidence radius.

Finally, the non-implication is witnessed inside the same class.  Let
\(P_n=P^0\) for every \(n\), where \(X\) is uniform on
\(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A\) is independent of \(X\) with
\(P^0(A=1)=1/2\), and \(Y(0)=Y(1)=Y=0\) almost surely.  Consistency and
conditional exchangeability hold by construction.  Fixed overlap holds
because \(\epsilon<1/2\); the cell-mean and conditional fourth-moment bounds
hold with value zero; and \(p_k=1/d\ge c_0/d\) because \(c_0\le1\).
The identifying functional and efficient-influence-function definition give
\(\tau(P^0)=0\) and \(\phi_{P^0}(O)=0\) almost surely, hence
\[
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)=0.                                         \tag{26}
\]
Consequently a statistic divided by \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)}\), a
variance ratio with denominator \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)\), and a Wald
endpoint comparison normalized by
\(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^0)/n}\) are undefined.  Since this sequence
satisfies every premise, those standardized, variance-ratio, or relative
endpoint conclusions do not follow on the stated class.  This witness makes
no claim about an absolute \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) endpoint comparison.
